summary: Agent 0.30.0 (ADR-0070). New routertls.go: routerTLSConfig(caFile) returns nil for an empty value (Go defaults with the system store, as before), otherwise a tls.Config with RootCAs = system pool (or an empty pool where none exists) plus the PEM certificates of the file and MinVersion TLS 1.2; hostname verification is unchanged; an unreadable file or one without a certificate is an error. RouterCfg gains ca_file; Config.validate calls routerTLSConfig so check-config and the start refuse an unusable file; app.go sets the result on the tunnel (websocket.Dialer TLSClientConfig) and the updater (download http.Client Transport with ProxyFromEnvironment). New setup_linux.go (build tag linux; setup_other.go now !windows && !linux): `setup [--router] [--update-key] [--ca-file] [--root]` refuses without root (unless --root), with a router URL not starting https://, an update key that is not 32 bytes base64, or an unusable CA file; writes the configuration only if none exists, owner-only with O_EXCL, with identity.dir /var/lib/skirnir-agent/identity, logging.dir /var/log/skirnir-agent and tunnel upstream on loopback; creates both folders 0700; copies os.Executable() to /usr/local/bin/skirnir-agent via a temporary file and rename; writes the go:embed unit; validates with loadConfig; without --root runs systemctl daemon-reload and enable --now; prints the fingerprint comparison step and STATE: installed. The unit's comments and description are English. The agent usage text is English and lists game (it said spiel).

findings.evidence: Nodes could reach a router with a private certificate only by installing that CA system-wide; Linux nodes had no setup and the README did not ask to compare fingerprints there.
findings.resolution: router.ca_file scoped to the router connection; Linux setup ends with the fingerprint comparison step.

findings.evidence: The Linux unit makes /etc read-only while the default key folder lived under /etc, and its writable folders had to pre-exist.
findings.resolution: setup places key and logs under /var and creates them 0700.

tests.command: go vet ./... (windows and GOOS=linux); go test -count=1 ./... on Windows and Linux (WSL)
tests.evidence: ok on both; new TestRouterTLSConfigInputs, TestTunnelDialTrustsOnlyWithCAFile, TestUpdateDownloadTrustsOnlyWithCAFile, TestConfigRefusesUnusableCAFile, TestLinuxSetupStaged, TestLinuxSetupRefusals ran (-v).
ok: the example with the commented ca_file still loads.

tests.command: All python test/... commands of ci.yml and security.yml (WSL); check_adr_index; selftest_english_names; ruff check .
tests.evidence: No failures; ADR index ok: 70 ADRs; ALLE OK; All checks passed.

limitations: systemctl enable --now runs only on a real Linux node; the staged test does not exercise it. A CA file on a node must be protected like the configuration.
Merged main after the PRs below it.
